label: Replay of documented requests, not a prediction

assumptions.name: Fire at the home
assumptions.value: the first documented fire within 200 m (about two blocks), leaving out sightings that are only about power lines
assumptions.why: the records date fire by block, not by house; power-line fires before midnight were mostly not the fire front (Citygate finding 12)

assumptions.name: Reaching the household
assumptions.why: households already known to need help are dialed first at about one call a second, and a call takes 2 to 4 minutes (dispatch/sim/constants.py)

assumptions.name: Approval and driver acceptance
assumptions.why: a dispatcher approves the offer and a driver accepts it on their phone

assumptions.name: Vans
assumptions.value: AccessLA vans, available from 4:00 a.m., leaving the Rose Bowl incident command post
assumptions.why: AccessLA said it was ready by 4 a.m. and was never called (LAist); the command post moved to the Rose Bowl at 8:52 p.m. (Citygate Table 2)

assumptions.name: Driving
assumptions.value: free-flow times on the OpenStreetMap road graph (data/roads/altadena.json)
assumptions.why: closures and smoke would slow vans; the margins below show how much slack each pickup had

assumptions.name: Boarding
assumptions.value: 20 min bedbound, 10 min wheelchair or disabled, 5 min elderly or unknown

assumptions.name: Order times west of Lake
assumptions.value: 3:25 a.m., or 5:42 a.m. for the Calaveras zone
assumptions.why: the Calaveras boundary isn't public, so every request is scored against both

assumptions.name: Earlier trigger
assumptions.value: calls to every household west of Lake that can't leave start at the first fire reported west of Lake, and AccessLA is asked at the same moment
assumptions.why: the timeline dates that report to 10:50 p.m., four and a half hours before the order; calling only households that can't leave displaces nobody else, and the system's job is to call the agency with vans

assumptions.name: Two finish lines
assumptions.value: a pickup counts against the first time the household had to ask for help, and separately against the first fire documented within two blocks
assumptions.why: many requests already say 'house on fire' or 'fire in yard', so beating the first request means the van arrived before the danger reached the door; the two-block line also counts spot fires that the household outlasted

fleetCheck.households: Synthetic population (data/population.json), west of Lake Avenue
fleetCheck.assumptions: one household per trip; the shelter is the drive-time origin for every return leg (roads treated as two-way); dialing at one call a second in deadline order
